method: MIXED. R1 and R2 are AMH's Rheumatoid arthritis topic and its Antirheumatics comparative table, paraphrased, no passage stored: the drug ladder and the dosing frequencies. S1 is an OPEN RACGP AJGP RESEARCH paper (May 2021) analysing a decade of BEACH data on how Australian GPs actually manage RA, quoted verbatim. It is used for two things AMH does not give: the GP's role and referral triggers as the RACGP guideline sets them, and what Australian practice actually looks like. ⚠️ S1 ITSELF NOTES THAT THE RACGP GUIDELINE IT REPORTS WAS ALREADY 10 YEARS OLD IN 2021, and that caveat is quoted and carried. NO DOSE APPEARS IN THIS GUIDELINE -- AMH's table gives FREQUENCIES, not doses, and no monograph was retrieved.

claims.claim: THE RACGP GUIDELINE'S DIAGNOSTIC AND INITIAL PLAN, as reported by this study: history, clinical examination and diagnostic investigations -- ESR and/or CRP, RHEUMATOID FACTOR and ANTI-CYCLIC CITRULLINATED PEPTIDE (CCP) ANTIBODY -- plus simple analgesics and NSAIDs having evaluated cardiovascular, gastrointestinal and renal status
claims.source_text: The RACGP guidelines recommend GPs undertake a diagnostic process - history, clinical examination and diagnostic investigations (ESR and/or CRP, RhF and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide [CCP] antibody) - and initial management plan (simple analgesics; NSAIDs, having evaluated cardiovascular, gastrointestinal and renal status).
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, RESEARCH, 'Characteristic-specific rates of rheumatoid arthritis and its management in Australian general practice', Volume 50 Issue 5, May 2021, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2021/may/rates-of-rheumatoid-arthritis-and-its-management-i, retrieved 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ THE REFERRAL TRIGGERS, as the study reports them from the RACGP guideline: RHEUMATOLOGIST REFERRAL SHOULD OCCUR IMMEDIATELY IF RHEUMATOID FACTOR AND/OR ANTI-CCP ANTIBODY IS POSITIVE, OR WITHIN SIX WEEKS AFTER PERSISTENT SWELLING IN MORE THAN ONE JOINT EVEN IF RHEUMATOID FACTOR IS NEGATIVE, OR IF NSAIDs OR STEROIDS ARE REQUIRED BEYOND SIX WEEKS after initial treatment -- with low-dose corticosteroids prescribed after consulting a rheumatologist, and DMARDs as early as possible for patients with poor prognosis
claims.source_text: If these fail, GPs are recommended to prescribe low-dose corticosteroids (after consulting a rheumatologist), and DMARDs as early as possible for patients with poor prognosis; rheumatologist referral should occur immediately if RhF and/or anti-CCP antibody is positive, or within six weeks after persistent swelling in more than one joint, even if RhF is negative, or if NSAIDs/steroids are required beyond six weeks after initial treatment.
claims.locator: RACGP, Australian Journal of General Practice, RESEARCH, 'Characteristic-specific rates of rheumatoid arthritis and its management in Australian general practice', Volume 50 Issue 5, May 2021, at https://www1.racgp.org.au/ajgp/2021/may/rates-of-rheumatoid-arthritis-and-its-management-i, retrieved 2026-09-22
